column2: Desiring prosperity, nourishment, or heaven, for destruction of sin, devoted to worship of the gods, the Krichchhra-doer is a sharer of all.
The gold-thief, liquor-drinker, Brahmin-killer and violator of the teacher's bed — having stolen or drunk liquor, a man should perform Krichchhra for a year.
For jewels, pearls, coral, copper, silver, iron, bronze and stones, twelve days eating grain-bits.
For taking men, women, field or house, wells, step-wells and tanks, the purification is remembered as Chandrayana.
For stealing edibles and foods, vehicles, beds and seats, flowers, roots and fruits, the five cow-products purify.
For grass, wood and trees, dry food, jaggery, cloth, hides and flesh, three nights' fasting.
One who goes to the father's wife, sister, teacher's daughter, teacher's wife or his own daughter is a violator of the teacher's bed.
For the teacher's bed, having confessed the sin, he should lie on a heated iron bed or embrace a red-hot statue; by death he is purified.
Or the violator of the teacher's bed may practice three months of Chandrayana. The same rule is to be done for fallen women too.
Whatever vow is for a man with another's wife, that vow should be made for her. Having cast seed in virgins, Chandalis and daughters,
or in the wives and offspring of sapindas, abandonment of life is prescribed. Whatever a twice-born does by one night's service to a Shudra woman,
eating alms and constantly repeating, he removes in three years. For going to an uncle's wife, brother's wife,
a Chandali or Pukkasi, daughter-in-law, sister, friend, mother's or father's sister, a deposited woman, one who sought refuge,
mother's brother's wife, sister, one of the same gotra desiring another, a disciple's wife or the teacher's wife, one should perform Chandrayana.
One who feels repentance after sin is done — for him the one atonement is the supreme remembrance of Hari.
Chandrayana, Paraka or Prajapatya removes floods of sin; repetition of mantras of the Sun, Ishvara, Shakti, Shri-Lord and the like removes floods of sin.
Recitation of the Gayatri, Om, hymns and mantras ends sin; with those beginning with Ka joined with seeds, the first and first with their endings;
the mantras of Sun, Ishvara, Shakti, Shri-Lord and others are over a crore, separately; "Om Hrim" beginning, ending in the dative, ending in "namah," give all desires.
The Narasimha twelve-syllable and eight-syllable garland-mantras remove floods of sin; reading and hearing the Agneya Purana and the like.
Vishnu is sung as of the form of the two knowledges, of the form of fire; the Supreme Self, the mouth of the gods, is sung in all the Vedas.
He is worshipped in engagement and in withdrawal, giver of enjoyment and liberation. Oblation, meditation and worship of Vishnu in fire form,
repetition, praise and bowing remove floods of all bodily sin. Ten golden gifts and the twelve grain gifts,
sixteen great gifts led by the Tulapurusha; the foremost gifts of food all remove sin.
On lunar day, weekday, star, transit, yoga and Manvantara-beginnings, vows and the like of the Sun, Ishvara, Shakti, Shri-Lord and others destroy sin.
Ganga, Gaya, Prayaga, Kashi, Ayodhya and Avanti, Kurukshetra, Pushkara, Naimisha, Purushottama,
Shalagrama, Prabhasa and the rest, sacred places that destroy floods of sin; "I am Brahman, supreme light" — this meditation removes floods of sin.
The Purana, Brahman and the Agneya; Brahma, Vishnu, Maheshvara; avatars; all worship; installation of images and the rest;
astronomy, Puranas, Smritis, austerity and vows; the science of wealth, creation and the rest, Ayurveda, archery;
phonetics, meter, grammar, etymology, lexicon, ritual, logic and Mimamsa — all else, Hari is the Lord.
He in whom the two are one, who knows all — seeing him, the sins of another perish; and he is Hari.
Hari is of the form of the eighteen knowledges, subtle, gross, and other; light, true imperishable Brahman, supreme Vishnu, stainless.
Cow-urine, cow-dung, milk, curds, ghee, kusha water, and a one-night fast is called Krichchhra Shantapana.
With each of the Shantapana substances separately, six days with fasting; in seven days this is Krichchhra; Mahashantapana destroys sin;
by a twelve-day fast Paraka destroys all sin; Maha-Paraka is told as three times this.
On the full moon fifteen mouthfuls, eating on the new moon; at decrease by one and then increase — Chandrayana; otherwise.
One should give a pala of the urine of a tawny cow, half a thumb of dung, seven palas of milk, two palas of curds,
one pala of ghee, one pala of kusha water. Cow-urine to be taken with the Gayatri; dung with "Gandhadvara";
milk with "Apyayasva"; curds with "Dadhikravna"; ghee with "Tejo'si"; kusha water with "Devasya."
Thus the Brahmakurcha becomes; one should recite the verse "Apo hi shtha"; joined with the Aghamarshana hymn or with Om,
having drunk it, freed from all sin, the faster goes to Vishnu's world. One who fasts, eats in the evening, an ascetic who eats at the sixth time,
avoids meat, performs the Ashvamedha and speaks truth goes to heaven. The fire-installation and consecration, sacrifices, gifts and vows,
Devavrata, bull-release, tonsure and girdle-tying, auspicious rites and anointing one should avoid in the intercalary month.
From new moon to new moon is the lunar month; thirty days the Savana; the solar month is from transit; the sidereal from the star's turning.
The solar month is for marriage and the like; the Savana for sacrifices and the like; the lunar month is praised in the yearly ancestral rite.
Taking Ashadhi as the limit, the fifth fortnight — one should perform the ancestral rite there, whether the sun goes to Virgo or not.
When in a month or a year there is doubling of lunar days, the later is to be known as the best; the earlier is the Malimluchi.
One should fast for that star by which the sun sets; lunar days are good by day for day-vows and at night for night-vows.
Even pairs; fire, made, element; six, sage; Vasu and openings; with Rudra the twelfth; fourteenth then full moon,
pratipada and the new moon: a pair of lunar days gives great fruit; when reversed it destroys, greatly terrible, merit earlier done.
For kings, ministers and vowers, in disturbances of marriage and the like, immediate purity is declared, in wilderness calamity, in assembly;
for those who have begun long austerities, a king is not a vow-breaker; for women pregnant, newly delivered, at night, virgin or menstruating,
when impure one should always have another do the acts. If a vow is broken through anger, negligence or greed,
one should not eat for three days, or shave the head. If unable to perform the vow, one should have the wife or a son do it.
In birth or death impurity the begun rite is left without worship; the teacher should revive the vowing, fainting person by drinking milk and the like.
Eight things do not break a vow: water, root, fruit, milk, oblation, Brahmin's wish, teacher's word and medicine.

For the increase of fame, offspring, knowledge, good fortune and health, for purity, enjoyment and liberation, I perform the vow, lord of vows.
agnipuran:175:45	This best vow has been taken by me before you; by your grace, lord of the world, may it reach unobstructed accomplishment.
agnipuran:175:46	If I die in this best vow being taken, while incomplete, let all that be complete, you being pleased, true lord.

I invoke the form of the vow, the glory of the world, in the mandala for all accomplishments; homage to you, be present, Keshava.
agnipuran:175:48	I bathe you with the five cow-products and with auspicious waters, with five nectars, imagined with mind and devotion; be the remover of my sin.
agnipuran:175:49	Lord of arghya, accept the auspicious arghya with scent, flowers and water, foot-water and rinsing; make me worthy of arghya always.
agnipuran:175:50	Lord of garments, accept the meritorious garment; make me always, covered with ornaments and fine garments, O true lord of the vow.
agnipuran:175:51	Accept the fragrant, pure scent, O form of fragrance; make me free of the scent of sin, make me fragrant.
agnipuran:175:52	Accept the flower; make me full of flowers always; the pure fragrance of flowers for increase of life and health.
agnipuran:175:53	Accept the ten-ingredient incense with guggulu and ghee; make me fumigated with incense, O true lord of fumigated.
agnipuran:175:54	Accept the lamp, with flame upward, shining, illuminating all; O form of the lamp, rich in light, always give me an upward goal.
agnipuran:175:55	Accept the food-offering of food and the rest, true lord of food; make me full of food, the giver of food and all gifts.
agnipuran:175:56	Whatever has been worshipped by me, O Lord, without mantra, without rite, without devotion, lord of vows, let it be complete for me.
agnipuran:175:57	Give dharma, give wealth, good fortune, a line of virtues; give fame, knowledge, life, heaven and liberation.
Having accepted this worship, lord of vows, go now, to return and to grant boons, O Lord.
The vower, having bathed, should in all vows worship the forms of the vow made of gold, according to ability, sleeping on the ground.
Repetition, oblation and gifts at the end of ordinary vows; twenty-four, or twelve, or five, or three, or one,
Brahmins and teachers are to be worshipped and fed; a fee is to be given according to ability; cows, gold and the like, and sandals and shoes separately,
a water vessel, a food vessel, clay, umbrella, seat, bed, a pair of garments, pots — this is the declared rule.

Likewise may my bond with my wife not be broken, god; as Lakshmi's bed is never empty of her, O boon-giver, Lord,
agnipuran:177:8	so may my bed too be never empty, Madhusudana. One should worship Lakshmi and Vishnu for a year and give a bed and fruits;
every month one should give arghya to Soma with a mantra: "Lamp of the sky's courtyard, born from the churning of the milk-ocean,
shining over the directions, younger brother of Rama, homage to you." "Om Shrim, homage to Shridhara" — one should worship Hari as the Self of the Moon;
Gham Dham Bham Ham, homage to Shri, to the ten-formed great Self. Oblation with ghee, and at night one should give a bed to a twice-born,
joined with lamp, food and vessels, umbrella, shoes and seat, a pot with water, an image and a vessel to a Brahmin.
The man who so does with his wife obtains enjoyment and liberation. I shall tell the Kanti vow: one should perform it in the bright half of Kartika;
eating at night on the second, one should worship Bala and Keshava; in a year one obtains radiance, life, health and the like.
Now I shall tell the Shishnu vow, giver of mental wishes: beginning with the bright second of Pausha, for four days,
first a bath with mustard, then with black sesame; on the third day with vacha; on the fourth with all herbs;
mura, mamsi, vacha, kushtha, shaileya, two turmerics, shati, champaka, musta — the group of all herbs is remembered.
One should worship with the names Krishna, Achyuta, Ananta, Hrishikesha; at the foot, navel, eye and in order on the head with flowers;
and give arghya to the moon with the names Shashi, Chandra, Shashanka, Indu. A man should eat at night as long as the moon stays;
for six months, a year, the vower obtains all purity. This vow was done by kings and women and gods earlier.
On the third of the bright half of Chaitra Gauri was married to Hara; having bathed with sesame one should worship Shambhu with Gauri with golden fruits and the like.
Homage to Patala — one should worship the feet of the Goddess and of Shiva; having chanted "to Shiva," one should worship the ankles with "to Jaya."
